paras: The lynching of David Cook was the killing of a young Black man by masked men in northern Kershaw County, South Carolina, in July 1882, after he was taken from officers who were conveying him to Camden. Cook, accused of attempted rape, was seized on Saturday, July 15, and his body was found two days later hanging from a tree. A Charleston wire report carried the story to papers across the country, most of them repeating its claim that he had confessed.

According to a Camden dispatch, an attempted rape took place on the night of Wednesday, July 12, in the northern part of Kershaw County. The victim's cries drew attention, pursuit was made, and 'circumstances pointed' to David Cook, described as 'a negro boy' who lived nearby. The Pickens Sentinel alone stated that the alleged victim was 'a young white girl'; no paper named her.

Cook was arrested on Saturday morning, July 15, and committed to jail. While two deputies were conveying him to Camden, about five and a half miles from the town, 'a party of masked men emerged from the woods' and took him from them. The Camden correspondent at first could learn nothing more, but on Monday, July 17, reported that the body had been found hanging from a tree several miles above the place where Cook was taken.

The Newberry Herald dated the lynching to 'Saturday night'. Both the Camden dispatch and the Charleston wire asserted that Cook had admitted his guilt, the Camden account adding that he said this 'was not the first case of the kind'; neither said to whom or under what conditions he spoke.

The Camden correspondent wrote that there was 'no excitement manifested here' and that 'very little interest' was shown in the section where the killing occurred. No report of an inquest, an arrest of any of the masked men, or a prosecution appears in the coverage.

The story reached most readers through a short Charleston dispatch dated July 17, which ran on July 18 in papers from Sacramento to Savannah and Washington. The wire stated as fact that Cook 'had attempted rape', said he was taken 'from the custody of the sheriff' by masked men, and closed with 'He confessed his guilt.' Headlines ranged from the plain 'Negro Lynched.' in Sacramento and 'LYNCHED' in Dallas to 'Summary Vengeance.' in the Savannah Morning News.

Reprinting garbled the place: the Dallas Daily Herald printed 'Crenshaw county', the Cambria Freeman 'Kershaw county, N.C.', and the Maysville Evening Bulletin put the lynching 'near Charleston'. Western roundups compressed the story further, the Cheyenne Daily Leader calling Cook 'guilty of an outrageous assault' and a Dakota paper describing him as 'a negro libertine' lynched 'on the 17th'.
Within South Carolina, the Anderson Intelligencer printed the fuller Camden letter under 'Lynching in Kershaw.', while the Pickens Sentinel ran a short item headed 'JUDGE LYNCH NEVER FAILS'.

The accounts differ on who held Cook: the Charleston wire named the sheriff, while the more detailed Camden dispatch and the Pickens Sentinel said he was taken from two deputies or constables on the road to Camden.

reader.title: Lynching of David Cook
bases: Masked men took David Cook, accused of attempted rape, from officers conveying him to Camden, and his body was found hanging from a tree (A13, A18, A3).

Cook was taken from custody by 'a party of masked men' and found hanged, with the papers tying the killing to an attempted-rape accusation (A13, A3, A18); no paper gives the number of men, but 'a party', 'a body of masked men' and 'a masked mob' describe a group (A13, A18, A2).

A Camden dispatch (A13) and a separate Charleston wire (A3, A14) agree that Cook, accused of attempted rape, was taken from custody by masked men on Saturday and lynched, though they differ on which officers held him.

accounts.label: Camden correspondent
accounts.gist: After an attempted rape Wednesday night, suspicion fell on Cook, who was arrested Saturday morning and seized by masked men from two deputies 5.5 miles from Camden; his body was found Monday hanging from a tree, and he reportedly admitted guilt.

accounts.label: Charleston wire
accounts.gist: Cook, who 'had attempted rape' in northern Kershaw County Wednesday, was taken from the sheriff Saturday by masked men and lynched; 'He confessed his guilt.'

framing.detail: Most papers ran the Charleston wire as a brief, stating the attempted rape as fact and adding 'He confessed his guilt', under headings such as 'Negro Lynched.' and 'LYNCHED'.
The Pickens Sentinel headed its item 'JUDGE LYNCH NEVER FAILS' and the Savannah Morning News 'Summary Vengeance.'
The Camden dispatch in the Anderson Intelligencer, 'Lynching in Kershaw.', reported the seizure and the local indifference without comment.
Distant roundups called Cook 'guilty of an outrageous assault' and 'a negro libertine'.

record_check.dossier: Arrested Saturday morning and 'committed to jail', he was seized from two deputies (constables) while being conveyed to Camden; no third officer is named, and the wire says 'the sheriff'.
No paper supports July 1; the papers give Saturday, July 15 for the seizure, July 17 for finding the body, and one roundup 'the 17th'.
Seized about 5.5 miles from Camden; hanged several miles above that place.
